newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares correct, seen bearish.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares correct, seen bearish.

text.p: Slovenian shares closed just higher on Wednesday, ending a nine day losing streak, but traders said they expected liquidity and volumes to remain poor in the short-term.
"There are no serious reasons for any rise. The correction could extend into next two days, but the downward trend is most likely to last over the summer," one broker said.
The SBI index rose 0.30 percent or 3.55 points to 1,193.85. So far this week the blue-chip index has fallen 3.4 percent.
Overall seven shares rose, seven fell and two were flat, while 13 were untraded. Turnover fell to 37.7 million tolars from 61.4 million.
Traders said volumes were likely to remain low, hampering the market's liquidity until fresh foreign portfolio investors resumed their activities.
In February the central bank ordered international investors to open custody accounts at local banks in order to be allowed to trade in securities.
Since then the index fell by over 27 percent while the average daily volume shrank to a tenth of its previous size.
Drug maker Lek had the highest turnover, easing 1.11 percent to 21,410 tolars on volume of 723 shares for total turnover of 15.4 million.
Health resort operator Terme Catez was the top gainer, jumping 5.32 percent to 11,690 tolars on volume of 145 shares.

"At these low volumes every purchase or sale moves shares significantly in either direction, there is no other explanation for such a rise in that share," Tomaz Logar, a trader at brokerage Start said.
Port operator Luka Koper was the top decliner, falling 5.67 percent to 1,580 tolars on volume of 861 shares, after the stock went ex-dividend.
